name: Earthtone III / Mr. DJ
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 crunk — Earthtone III / Mr. DJ
notes: The self-production company — the Dungeon Family sound with the band replaced by the group's own writing — so where the OutKast entry is a performance, this one is a **board**, and the two are separated on exactly that. Four parameters do it. (1) **The kit is programmed with live overdubs, not a live kit with programmed snares**: `humanize.quantizeStrength` climbs to 0.78 against the OutKast entry's 0.6, and `velocityVar` drops to 0.2. (2) **The drum bus is an effect target**, which the research states outright — slap delay and plate reverb on the snare. A send is not in the schema, but what a slap-delayed snare *does* to the grid is: `snare.offGridMs` [8,18] pushes it well behind the beat (the parent sits at [2,7]) and the snare's `timingJitterMs` rises to 14, so the backbeat smears rather than snaps. This is the honest half of an effect claim, and it is labelled as such. (3) **Harmony is stated, not implied** — the paragraph's own phrase — so `chords.impliedByRiff` is explicitly false and the documented I–IV–V–VI in G major carries the top weight, spelled with VI rather than vi because the deceptive cadence *is* that chord. Modal mixture is `borrowed.V` 0.34; the minor 7/9 vamps are `extensions.ninth` 0.30. (4) **The metric game is the signature here more than anywhere.** `melody.phraseBars` puts 6 at weight 5 — the highest weight any single phrase length gets in this batch — for the documented meter change on the fourth measure of each six-measure phrase, "22 quarter note beats per phrase". ⛔ **The signature figure itself is still not in this file.** The schema has no time signature and no per-phrase meter; six-bar phrases in 4/4 are the reachable half, and the other half is absent rather than approximated. Beat switches and skits are `switchUpProb` 0.55, the highest here; the long tag outros are a 12–16 bar outro that decays with the countermelody still in it. `bpm` spans 68–160 because the paragraph gives both the early 68–100 and the 159 of the 2003 single. ⚠ **Confidence is high, and that is the research's rating** — the company's formation, the tempo, key, progression and phrase-length device are all sourced. What is a reading rather than a quote: the `offGridMs` and jitter numbers above, and `glideProb` 0.12, which is the "synth bass performed by a session keyboardist" heard as portamento. `timbreHint` is `spacey_keys` for the "outer space-influenced production with echo and reverb effects"; the vocoder-treated vocal stacks (30–40 takes per line) are the countermelody, which is why `densityRatio` is 0.8 — the fullest in this batch — and `fillGapsOnly` is false. This model's fill band is `smallEveryBars` 2 / `bigEveryBars` 4 with a 16th/32nd strong-weak roll; inside it, `descendProb` 0.65 is the highest of the seven and `gapProb` 0.16 among the lowest, so its roll falls where its siblings' climb. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.3 to 0.47.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.3 over this model's 12-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [51, 87] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 44 against a bass reaching 50, an overlap of 7. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.8, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn.
